value.note: VERDICT: APPROVE WITH NOTES. No CRITICAL and no HIGH code defect. Every code-side acceptance clause decidable read-only decides TRUE at source, including all four packet-named least-confident areas. The one HIGH (F001) was an EVIDENCE gap, never a code defect, and it is CLOSED: it was raised when no green full gate bound to the frozen SHA and the newest executed gates were RED at e6a2d5d5, then closed within this same review when the PM landed assets/rust-gate-335d-green.txt, assets/engineering-gate-335d-green.json and assets/final-gates-proof.json — both gates exit 0 on 335d2098, no required sensor skipped, verified by me at the raw output rather than at the receipt (see verdict row V001). The F001 finding text is retained verbatim as the historical record of what was true when it was raised; its resolution is fixed. Open at close: F002 and F003 (traceability only, PM-owned and accepted for bounded correction) and F004 (latent, unreachable). F005 is refuted at source. Production/chainglass arms (AC2, AC3, AC7, AC9 and tk-42a4) remain prime-owned and correctly blocked, never fabricated green. Accepted local code is not production or whole-plan acceptance. Full A-H report: ./review.final-composed.md; subject code diff: ./_computed.diff (150 non-doc files, docs/** excluded); reviewed-file manifest: ./_computed.manifest.txt. Review was strictly read-only: no builds, tests, formatters, linters, commits, daemon actions or source edits.

value.finding: No captured green full gate binds to the frozen subject SHA 335d20981c37c868f6039724f4a78b621c8bb7e2. The newest executed full gates in the repository are RED at the prior revision e6a2d5d5: assets/rust-gate-e6a2-red.txt records `test result: FAILED. 31 passed; 1 failed` with `daemon_death_mid_stage_restores_input_within_bound` panicking at crates/tmux/tests/adapter.rs:1217, and assets/engineering-gate-e6a2-red.txt records `1 check(s) failed: test`. No artifact anywhere under docs/plans/139-rs-governance-port references 335d2098 (grep count zero). This is an evidence gap, not a code defect: I independently verified that 335d2098 is test/fixture-only (crates/tmux/tests/adapter.rs and .pi/extensions/pij/cli.integration.test.ts, plus assets) and that neither change weakens an assertion — the 2s recovery bound is retained at crates/tmux/tests/adapter.rs:570, the pane observation now asserts command success and rejects non-boolean output, and the inbox-register case moves from a blanket closed-verb list to a stricter explicit assertion (exit 4, details.code E-AMBIG, exactly one GET /health, legacy snapshot unchanged, no tmux). Smallest fix: the PM records the raw pij-gate and `harness checks --json` output for 335d2098 under assets/. Nothing else is required to close this.

value.finding: Phase-1 and phase-2 tasks are marked `checked` while citing receipt commit 0a7a26737d08701bddac6ccc0b6d7b040873e4f9, a wave-1 checkpoint superseded by the main merge (d0cd734c), the u4/u5 composition (5eda7fc2), and the later revisions 78531a0b, e6a2d5d5 and 335d2098. Affected: tk-11a1, tk-12a1 (phase-1) and tk-20a2, tk-21a2, tk-22a2 (phase-2). The links themselves resolve — this is staleness, not a dangling pointer — but 'checked' therefore asserts regression-freedom against a pre-merge state rather than against the composed artifact under review. Smallest fix: re-point those receipts at the composed execution entries (execution-log.dd.json#entries/lg-0009 and lg-0012).

value.finding: crates/testkit/fixtures/golden/api/governance-client-parity.json declares `source_base: 78531a0ba2f22469ab72289ba9ff6c1635e863e7`, but every one of the 30 files listed in its `source_snapshot` changed between that commit and the frozen SHA. I verified the digests directly (`sha256sum -c` over the pinned map): 30/30 match the frozen worktree, so the pinned corpus IS the reviewed artifact's corpus and the parity evidence is sound — but a consumer who resolves `source_base` to fetch the compared bytes gets different content than the fixture pins. The fixture's own `history` field already carries `previous_capture_commit` with the same value, which is what `source_base` appears to actually mean. Smallest fix: set `source_base` to the real capture commit, or rename the field to match its meaning.
value.note: The parity claim itself stands: 66 matched pairs, comparison declared as original UTF-8 stdout with no normalization.

value.finding: Relay-line rendering diverges from the legacy text in two spellings that are unreachable today. crates/core/src/anomalies.rs:131-139 renders multi-sequence evidence with `.join(",")` and empty evidence as `"none"`, while the legacy renderer at .pi/extensions/pij/core/daemon/anomaly-sweep.ts:133 uses `.join(", ")` and `|| "(none)"`. I disproved the material form of this before reporting it: every detector in crates/core/src/anomalies.rs (lines 339, 380, 418, 479, 511) emits exactly one sequence, so neither the multi-seq nor the empty branch can fire, and AC5's byte-for-byte relay parity holds for every reachable input — the golden samples in governance-routes.json all carry a single `spine <seq>`. Recorded as a latent trap, not a live defect: the first detector that emits zero or two sequences silently breaks byte parity for supervisors and PA scripts that grep these lines.
value.note: Below the material bar by the packet's own rule; recorded because the failure mode is silent and the cost of alignment is two characters.

value.finding: A read-only critic reported as HIGH that `AnomalyThresholds::default()` hardcodes a 10-minute status-stale threshold instead of referencing the named constant, which would contradict AC5's 30-minute policy and its single-owner clause. value.finding: ADDENDUM (bounded metadata delta, post-verdict). In the corrected plan.dd.json every newly checked acceptance criterion — AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC8 — carries `proven_by: assets/execution-log.dd.json#entries/lg-0015`, and lg-0015 is the entry recording THIS REVIEW. A review is a judgement about evidence, not evidence: it executes nothing. AC1 is the sharpest case, because its text demands a live two-subscriber control observing a `report now` frame and an `adopt` seat.put written while open — an execution that genuinely exists (the isolated-daemon control captured in green-proof-wave1.json / native-cli-workflow-proof.json) but is now not what the AC points at. My own AC1 verdict was 'TRUE (code + isolated)', which is a reading of that control, not a re-run of it; citing my opinion as the proof makes this review load-bearing for acceptance in a way I did not assert and cannot support. Note the same document does this correctly elsewhere: every backpressure row and every task/done_when row cites lg-0014, an actual gate execution. Smallest fix: point each checked AC's `proven_by` at the executed entry carrying its witness (the live-control, CLI-workflow, parity and dual-gate entries), and keep lg-0015 as a corroborating `links` reference rather than the proof.
value.note: Raised after the APPROVE WITH NOTES verdict, against the metadata-only correction delta. Does not change that verdict; no runtime code is involved.

value.finding: ADDENDUM (process). The correction was announced to me as bounded — F002 rebinding five checked tasks/assertions to lg-0014, and F003 renaming the corpus label — but the delta I re-reviewed also flips state from `unchecked` to `checked` on tk-30a3, tk-31a3, tk-32a3 and tk-40a4, on their done_when assertions and backpressure rows bp-0005..bp-0008, on phase ph-e6f8, and on five acceptance criteria in plan.dd.json. Those are acceptance decisions, not traceability corrections. On the merits I can support each one: the phase-3 tasks have prior named RED/GREEN plus the composed dual-green; tk-40a4's AC8 surface is entirely local and its guard is real; AC1/AC4/AC5/AC6/AC8 are the five ACs I judged TRUE with no prime-owned arm; and the four ACs with production or chainglass arms (AC2, AC3, AC7, AC9) plus tk-41a4, tk-42a4 and phase ph-a9c3 were correctly left unchecked or blocked. So this is a scope-declaration defect, not a false claim — but a reviewer who had ACKed only the announced bound would have ACKed more than was described.
value.note: Recorded for the record and because the same pattern at a larger scale is how an unproven state flip enters a plan unnoticed.

value.finding: FINAL PIN. `tk-41a4` and its assertion `dw-41a4` are now `checked` citing `execution-log.dd.json#entries/lg-0015` — this review — and three things about that pairing do not line up in the artifacts. (1) The assertion `dw-41a4` reads verbatim `RED named on the pre-fix tree, GREEN after; receipt = commit + test names + live seqs where the task has a live arm.` A review satisfies none of those clauses: there is no RED, no GREEN, no test names and no live seqs. For the sibling `tk-40a4` the identical assertion IS satisfied, by `lg-0014`, a real gate run. (2) `dw-41a4` carries `pressure: bp-0009`, and `bp-0009` is still `unchecked`. The record therefore asserts the assertion satisfied while the pressure row it names says the criterion is not, with nothing on the page reconciling them. (3) `tk-41a4.note` is `null`, and `lg-0015`'s own text contains no wording marking it as corroborating judgement rather than execution — I grepped it. So the distinction that makes this defensible exists only in the IRC message to me, not in any artifact a later reader will resolve. Smallest fix, either one: add a note to `tk-41a4`/`dw-41a4` naming the actual instrument (independent cross-model documentation inspection, plus AC9's own legacy-verb grep returning zero across the ported rows) and scoping the check explicitly to the documentation half; or leave `dw-41a4` unchecked until `bp-0009` can close with its prime-owned arm.
value.note: Also a self-disclosure: see verdict row V008 for the exact strength of the judgement being leaned on here.

value.rationale: Refuted at source. crates/core/src/anomalies.rs:220-227 reads: `impl Default for AnomalyThresholds { fn default() -> Self { Self { status_stale_ms: STATUS_STALE_MS, delivered_unacked_stale_ms: 15 * 60 * 1_000 } } }`. The default references the named constant declared at line 22 (`pub const STATUS_STALE_MS: u64 = 30 * 60 * 1_000;`). The quoted `10 * 60 * 1_000` does not exist at that location. AC5's single-owner clause holds: one named crates/core constant owns the anomaly threshold, and the only other 30-minute literals in the file are test boundary values at lines 639, 652, 846 and 874. The separate 10-minute per-command stderr nudge is a different mechanism and is untouched.
value.note: Recorded to keep the refutation citable; rank played no part — the code was read.

value.rationale: Re-reviewed at the delta and accepted. The five rows now carry `receipt: ../../execution-log.dd.json#entries/lg-0014` in place of the superseded `0a7a2673; …#entries/lg-0002`, and their assertions replace `pressure: not-applicable` with real rows (bp-0001, bp-0003, bp-0004). lg-0014 exists and is an execution entry, not a claim: it records the canonical Rust gate at exit 0 across all six stages with a 9-crate zero-violation architecture pass, and the complete engineering checks at exit 0 with no skips at 2026-09-07T14:59:32.894Z, naming the three raw artifacts. The original notes and the historical logs are retained rather than overwritten, so the earlier RED/GREEN lineage is still readable.

Re-reviewed at the delta and accepted; the implementation is better than the fix I proposed. Rather than renaming the corpus key and leaving two labels saying the same thing, the PM deleted the redundant `source_base` outright because `history.previous_capture_commit` already records the 78531a0b lineage correctly, and renamed the only `source_base` in the parity RECEIPT to `previous_capture_commit`. I verified the claim of byte-equality rather than accepting it: the fixture diff is exactly one deleted line; MANIFEST.toml moves 112803 -> 112742 bytes, a 61-byte delta equal to that line, with sha256 a9311375… -> 8ac16285…, which matches `sha256sum` of the file on disk; `diff <(git show HEAD:… | jq -S 'del(.source_base)') <(jq -S . …)` reports IDENTICAL, so every captured stdout byte, every pair and every count is unchanged; and all 30 `source_snapshot` digests still verify against the frozen tree (30/30 OK). The parity receipt keeps the original capture digest under `captured_corpus_sha256` alongside the corrected one, and assets/review-traceability-correction.json records the change with `runtime_source_changed: false` — which the diff confirms: the only non-doc files touched are the fixture and its manifest digest.
value.note: Closed. Provenance is strictly better than before: the old capture identity is retained, not overwritten.

value.rationale: Verified in the corrected document: `jq '.sections[]|select(.name=="acceptance_criteria")|.value[]|"\(.id) \(.state) \(.proven_by)"'` returns lg-0015 for each of AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6 and AC8, and lg-0015 is the execution-log entry describing this review's verdict. The distinction is not pedantic: it is the plan's own doctrine that a receipt is not proof, and an AC whose proof pointer resolves to a reviewer's opinion cannot be re-derived by anyone who does not trust that reviewer. The correct executions exist and are already cited elsewhere in the same correction, which is why this is a pointer defect rather than an evidence gap.
value.note: PM-owned, cheap to fix, and does not disturb the APPROVE WITH NOTES verdict.

value.rationale: Confirmed as a scope-declaration defect and explicitly NOT as a false or unproven claim. I checked each flip against its evidence before deciding: the four newly checked tasks and the five newly checked ACs are ones I had already judged TRUE on local/isolated grounds, the backpressure rows correctly cite the gate execution lg-0014, and every criterion with a prime-owned arm (AC2, AC3, AC7, AC9) plus tk-41a4, tk-42a4 and phase ph-a9c3 remains unchecked or blocked — tk-42a4 still reads `blocked`, exactly as ruled. The finding stands because the announced bound and the delivered delta differed, and a bounded ACK given on the announcement alone would have covered acceptance decisions it did not describe.
value.note: No re-work requested; state the full scope when announcing the next delta.
